title: Renderer core: device, frame graph with scene copies, G-buffer, lighting, body-anchored shadows, post, mesh system, lab harness
brief:
PROJECT: true-scale Earth/Moon spaceflight simulator on raw WebGPU (desktop Chrome/Edge, RTX 5090). Repo C:\dev\fable-space-game. BEFORE CODING read in full: PROMPT.txt (binding user requirement), docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (binding; wins over research docs; sections 4, 10 and 17 are yours to implement), docs/PACKAGE_RULES.md, src/core/contracts/*.ts, and the docs under READ.

RULES (full text in docs/PACKAGE_RULES.md, binding): (1) Edit only your ownedPaths; src/core, tests/browser/harness.ts and other teams' paths are read-only - if a contract is wrong or lacking, work within your paths, file docs/requests/render-core-<n>.md and list it in your hand-off. (2) No placeholders, stubs, TODOs or 'simplified for now'. (3) `npx vitest run tools/dev/boundaries.test.ts` stays green. (4) Shared tree: verify with scoped commands only (`npm run typecheck:paths -- <paths>`, `npx vitest run <paths>`, `npx playwright test tests/browser/render-core --project=functional`; perf specs are *.perf.spec.ts, run with --project=perf and measure inside withGpuLock). Never `npm run build`; leave no server or browser running. Git: only `git add <your paths>` + commit; never add -A/stash/reset/checkout; never commit .env or data/tiles|sky|cache. (5) Write tool for files (heredocs break on Windows); absolute paths. (6) Timings measured while the data bakes run are provisional: record them, do not loosen budgets. (7) Browser work follows labs/template + tests/browser/shell/lab-template.spec.ts (assertDiscreteGpu, expectNoErrors, saveScreenshot), then LOOK at each PNG (Read it) and iterate until it is convincing. (8) Finish with docs/handoff/render-core.md.

READ: docs/research/rendering-design.md (all; you own sections 1-3, 8, 11, 13 and the infrastructure every other section needs; where it disagrees with ARCHITECTURE sections 10 and 17, the architecture wins), docs/research/webgpu-harness.md (limits, gotchas), src/core/contracts/render.ts, src/core/gpu/device.ts.

ORDER OF WORK: seven render packages build on your API the moment you finish, and it is reviewed first. Build and COMMIT milestone A before starting milestone B. A = the complete frame graph with every hook callable and every core copy in place, bind group 0, shader library with all chunks (shadow and AO terms returning 1 until B), G-buffer + basic deferred lighting, mesh system, all SharedResources defaults, the lab app with LabPlanet, and a complete first docs/RENDER_API.md. B = shadows, AO/contact shadows, the full lighting model, TAA/TAAU + dynamic resolution, bloom, auto-exposure, tonemap, the quality governor, perf attribution, then the final RENDER_API.md.

SCOPE - implement in src/render/core:
1. `createRenderer(canvas, gpu: GpuHandle, defs, opts): Promise<Renderer>` implementing the `Renderer`, `RenderContext`, `FrameContext`, `SharedResources`, `ShaderLibrary`, `PerfRecorder` contracts. FrameContext is built in float64: camera-relative BodyPose/VesselPose (current + previous), rotation-only view, `mat4.perspectiveReversedZInfinite` with Halton-8 jitter added to clip xy, prevViewProj/prevEyeOffset, sun (direction, illuminance from BodyDef.emission and distance, angular radius), exposure, qualityScale. Poses come from the snapshot as given (the sim already interpolates them to presentation time: SimSnapshot.ut).
2. Frame graph exactly as the table in ARCHITECTURE 10.0, including the core rows: 'scene.depthOpaque' (copy of the depth attachment after the G-buffer), 'scene.colorCopy' (HDR after deferred lighting, before drawWater), 'scene.depth' (depth after drawWater), 'scene.depthHalf' (half-resolution rg32float, r = min and g = max reversed-Z of each 2 x 2 block), 'scene.colorCopyTransparent' (HDR after preTransparent). Colour copies are made only when a registered feature lists the key in `requires`. Hooks: prepare, compute, drawShadow, drawGBuffer, drawWater, drawBackground, compositeAtmosphere, preTransparent, drawTransparent, drawOverlay, each over features in ascending `order` then registration order. Targets per RENDER_FORMATS: G-buffer RT0 albedo, RT1 normal, RT2 material, RT3 velocity, RT4 extra, plus HDR emissive, and reversed-Z depth32float (compare greater, clear 0). Attachments, read-only depth and compare functions per hook exactly as the table states. A live attachment is never bound for sampling.
3. Bind group 0 (frame uniforms incl. per-body sphere/atmosphere parameters from BodyDef.render for up to 4 bodies, eclipse occluder list, shared samplers, blue noise). maxBindGroups is 4: document the group plan (frame / pass / material / object).
4. ShaderLibrary with `#include "name"`, compile-error capture into window.__test.errors, and these documented chunks: frame (frame uniforms; `writeHdr(rgb)` = clamp to HDR_MAX with NaN and negatives removed, used by every HDR write of yours and mandatory for features); gbuffer (encode/decode of all five targets, octahedral normals, `tangentFrame(n)` and tangent-angle packing for RT4, `encodeWaterDepth`/`decodeWaterDepth` per WATER_DEPTH_ENCODE_MAX, the MATERIAL_PARAM meanings); brdf (GGX height-correlated in isotropic and anisotropic form + Burley + multiscatter compensation, clearcoat, sheen/translucency); shadows (`sampleSunShadow`); atmosphere_common (Bruneton (r, mu) LUT parameterisation, the stable `altitudeAt`, and `aerialSliceToDistance`/`aerialDistanceToSlice` for the 32^3 'atmosphere.aerialPerspective' volume); transparency (`applyAtmosphere(uv, distance, colour, alpha)`: adds in-scatter and applies transmittance from the aerial volume up to `distance`, and attenuates fragments farther than 'clouds.depth' by 'clouds.screen'.a with a soft transition; exactly neutral with the default resources); eclipse (circle-overlap fraction of the solar disc); noise; HASH_WGSL from src/core. Three OVERRIDABLE chunks with fixed documented signatures and working defaults: `brdf_water` (GGX F0 0.02, Cox-Munk unresolved slope variance, sky reflection, depth colour from decodeWaterDepth), `brdf_terrain` (Lambert + low GGX), `brdf_regolith` (the Hapke function of rendering-design 8.2 with the albedo->w inversion LUT). Registering a chunk again replaces it and rebuilds dependent pipelines.
5. Sun shadows per ARCHITECTURE 10.1: up to 8 logarithmic cascades (12 m .. 1500 km), 2048^2 depth32float array, staggered updates. Every cascade is fitted, anchored and texel-snapped in the body-fixed frame of the body it covers (nearest surface), or the active vessel's frame for cascade 0 in cockpit view; `ShadowCascadeView.viewProj` and 'shadow.uniforms' are re-derived EVERY frame in float64 as capture matrix x motion of the anchor frame since capture, so staggered cascades stay registered to ground that moves 7-30 m per frame in ROOT axes. Set `anchor`, `everyFrame`, `fit` on every ShadowCascadeView; call drawShadow only for cascades re-rendered this frame; at least the two nearest cascades are everyFrame. When a terrain body lies wholly beyond the last camera-fitted cascade, refit the far cascade to that body's sunlit disc (`fit: 'body'`, one per visible terrain body) with a continuous hand-over on approach. PCSS-lite filtering with the true solar angular size, normal-offset + slope bias. Screen-space contact shadows and GTAO at half resolution.
6. Deferred lighting: sun x transmittance (sampled from 'atmosphere.transmittanceLut' with the body parameters; default LUT = white) x eclipse x cloud shadow ('clouds.shadowMap' near + 'clouds.coverageMap' far; defaults = no cloud); ambient from 'atmosphere.skyIrradianceLut'; IBL from 'env.probeCube'/'env.sh9' (defaults black); planetshine computed by you on the CPU from the snapshot (Lambert-sphere phase, BodyDef.render.meanColor/geometricAlbedo) as directional fills; local lights from FrameContext.lights (point/capsule, inverse square); material branches by MATERIAL_ID with the parameter meanings of MATERIAL_PARAM; anisotropy and clearcoat from RT4 for standard materials; emissive. Eclipses and planetshine are YOURS (no other package implements them).
7. Post: TAA/TAAU (closest-depth velocity dilation, YCoCg variance clip, Catmull-Rom history, RCAS) with dynamic resolution driven by GPU timestamps; history handling under warp (rendering-design 2.4); threshold-free bloom; TAA and bloom sanitise their inputs (NaN/Inf to 0, clamp to HDR_MAX). Auto-exposure per ARCHITECTURE 10.4: histogram over lit geometry only (depth == 0 and pixels under an absolute luminance floor excluded), mean of the lit range to mid-grey with a cap keeping the 99th percentile of lit pixels below about 4x mid-grey, photometric prior when under 0.5 % of the frame is lit (sunny-16 scaled by sun visibility when a lit body or vessel is in view, dark-adapted floor otherwise), honouring CameraState.exposureCompensation/minEv100 and interior metering when CameraState.kind is 'interior'. AgX tonemap + dither; then the LDR overlay pass. Quality governor: FrameContext.qualityScale (0.5..1) lowered when GPU time nears the 11 ms budget and restored with hysteresis, acting before dynamic resolution; 1 in deterministic mode.
8. Mesh system for every other package: upload ModelData (MeshData + PbrMaterialDef incl. anisotropy and clearcoat into RT4), texture loading with mips (webp/png URLs and procedural textures), instanced draws into G-buffer and shadow passes with camera-relative per-instance transforms (current + previous for velocity), per-instance parameters (temperature for blackbody emissive, soot, frost, wetness, dither fade), LOD pick by projected size with dithered cross-fade, Kaplanyan specular AA, and a per-draw flag telling whether the caster is body-fixed (all cascades) or moving (everyFrame cascades only).
9. Utilities features need: fullscreen-triangle helper, half-res targets, depth-aware 4-tap upsample from 'scene.depthHalf', mip generation, GPU timestamp pooling, `readHdrStats`, OOM error scopes on large allocations.
10. Lab support used by ALL wave-2 render teams: `createLabApp({ canvas, scene | sim, features })` in src/render/core/lab that boots GPU + defs + FakeSim (or a given Sim), provides a simple free/orbit camera placeable by query string (body + lat/lon/alt/heading/pitch, or vessel-relative offset) and by window.__test.setCameraOrbit, sets CameraState.kind, accepts any number of features, and wires the full TestApi (isIdle, perf, hdrStats, setDeterministic, setPaused). Plus `createLabPlanetFeature()`: an analytically ray-traced sphere per body written to the G-buffer with correct depth (albedo from the tile set's `albedoLowRes` global map when present; MATERIAL_ID.water with an encoded depth where that map is ocean-coloured), honouring 'ocean.nearField' the way the real terrain will (discard the water where the eye distance is below fadeStart, drawing a seabed sphere 30 m below instead), as a precise planet-scale backdrop for labs only.
11. window.__perf (PerfSnapshot) with per-pass GPU ms, CPU ms, counters and the per-feature breakdown `features`. Timestamp queries exist only at pass boundaries, so provide an attribution mode (renderer option and `?perf=features`) in which each feature's hook inside a core-owned pass (shadow, G-buffer, water, background, transparent) runs in its own pass with loadOp 'load'; perf specs use it.
12. docs/RENDER_API.md: exact WGSL struct layouts, bind group 0 layout, G-buffer write/read helpers for all five targets, chunk list and override signatures, how to write a RenderFeature for each hook (attachments, load/store, blend rules, which scene copy to sample when), cascade rules for casters, mesh system API, lab app API, perf attribution, photometric conventions with worked numbers (sun 128,000 lux; sunlit ground about 10^4 cd/m^2; exposure formula; HDR_MAX).

ACCEPTANCE: a lab scene (labs/render-core) with FakeSim scenes showing a PBR material sweep including anisotropic and clearcoat rows, shadowed geometry on a ground slab, emissive objects, a vessel-sized object near the camera 6,371 km from the origin and a Moon-sized sphere 384,400 km away in the same frame with no z-fighting or jitter while the camera moves (prove sub-millimetre stability: frame diff of a static scene with TAA is below 1/255 mean). HDR readback: sun-lit white Lambert surface within 10% of E*albedo/pi*exposure; no NaN. Overflow: with exposure forced to EV100 -3, bring the sun disc and a mirror-like metal sphere into view: nanPixels == 0 on every frame and the image recovers as exposure adapts. Exposure: a sunlit object covering 3 % of an otherwise black frame, and a thin crescent of a body, both expose within 0.5 EV of the sunny-16 value; a fully dark frame reaches the dark-adapted floor; exposure adapts between a sunlit and an eclipsed scene. Shadows: contact-hardening visible, no acne at 85 deg sun incidence; in the FakeSim `pad` scene (Earth rotating, casters fixed in the body frame) and in the `lunarOrbit` scene flying 1.6 km/s over body-fixed casters, the frame-to-frame difference along shadow edges stays below a bound you justify and shows no period-2/4/8 pattern from staggered cascades; a vessel-frame caster never appears in a staggered cascade; with the camera 20,000 km from a Moon-sized LabPlanet carrying a body-fixed test ridge, the ridge's shadow is visible at the terminator, and an approach through 1,500 km shows no pop. Frame graph: a test feature per hook proves order, attachments, that 'scene.depthOpaque'/'scene.depth'/'scene.depthHalf' hold this frame's values in the hooks the contract names, and that colour copies exist only when required; a half-resolution volume rendered in preTransparent and composited in drawTransparent is correctly occluded by opaque geometry. `applyAtmosphere` is neutral with defaults and hides a transparent quad behind a synthetic cloud layer published by the lab. Dynamic resolution and the governor hold 60 fps when the lab adds a deliberately heavy pass (governor first). Perf at 1440p internal (ARCHITECTURE 17.1 'core fixed' line): AO + contact 0.6, lighting 1.0, TAA 0.55, bloom 0.3, tonemap/exposure 0.2, copies + depth pyramid 0.35 = 3.0 ms p99 in total; lab scene with 1.5 M triangles: G-buffer + amortised shadows under 2.0 ms; CPU frame under 2 ms. All default SharedResources work with no feature present; overriding a brdf chunk at runtime works. Unit tests for CPU maths (jitter, cascade fitting and body-frame snapping with per-frame matrix re-derivation in f64, camera-relative poses, exposure curve and metering rules, governor hysteresis). Zero uncaptured GPU errors.

SELF-VERIFY: specs in tests/browser/render-core (functional + *.perf.spec.ts under withGpuLock), screenshots in out/screens/render-core reviewed by eye, `npm run typecheck:paths -- src/render/core labs/render-core tests/browser/render-core tests/unit/render-core`, `npx vitest run src/render/core tests/unit/render-core tools/dev/boundaries.test.ts`.

title: CPU terrain height authority: tile sources, coverage-blended height function, procedural amplification, craters, rocks
brief:
PROJECT: true-scale Earth/Moon spaceflight simulator on raw WebGPU. Repo C:\dev\fable-space-game. BEFORE CODING read in full: PROMPT.txt, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (binding; sections 4 and 7), docs/PACKAGE_RULES.md, src/core/contracts/*.ts, and the docs under READ.

RULES (full text in docs/PACKAGE_RULES.md, binding): (1) Edit only your ownedPaths; src/core and other teams' paths are read-only - file docs/requests/terrain-core-<n>.md and list needed contract changes in your hand-off instead of editing. (2) No placeholders, stubs, TODOs. (3) Your code is headless and deterministic: no DOM, no WebGPU, no timers, no Math.random/Date/performance; `npx vitest run tools/dev/boundaries.test.ts` stays green. Node builtins only in a module named fsTileSource.ts (or *.node.ts) that browser code never imports. (4) Shared tree: verify with `npm run typecheck:paths -- src/terrain tests/unit/terrain-core tools/terrain-core` and `npx vitest run src/terrain tests/unit/terrain-core tools/dev/boundaries.test.ts`; never `npm run build`; git only `git add <your paths>` + commit; never commit .env or data/tiles|sky|cache. (5) Write tool for files; absolute paths. (6) Timings measured while the data bakes run are provisional: record them with the load noted, do not loosen budgets. (7) Finish with docs/handoff/terrain-core.md (public API with signatures, measured timings, limits, change requests).

READ: docs/research/rendering-design.md sections 4.5-4.8, docs/research/moon-sky-data.md section 4 (crater, regolith, rock statistics; constants tagged [unverified] must be checked or calibrated, not trusted), docs/research/sim-design.md section 9.1, src/core/contracts/terrain.ts (the TerrainProvider doc comment and the COVERAGE_BLEND_TILES comment are your specification), src/core/geo/*.ts, src/core/math/hash.ts.

SCOPE - src/terrain implements the single height authority used by physics, by the renderer's tile workers and by rock placement:
1. TileSource implementations: `createFetchTileSource(baseUrl)` (browser + workers) and, in the node-only module src/terrain/fsTileSource.ts, `createFsTileSource(rootDir)`; manifest caching; `layerHasTile` decides existence (never request unpromised tiles).
2. Decoded-tile cache (byte-budgeted LRU, pinned resident level, pins per named slot as in `ensureLoaded(body, dir, radius, slot)`: a new call for the same slot replaces that slot's pin) with synchronous lookup; async loading; eviction order depends only on the sequence of calls, never on timing; works identically on the main thread and inside a worker.
3. `createTerrainProvider(defs, tileSource, opts): Promise<TerrainProvider & RockField & TerrainBaker>` implementing the TerrainProvider contract EXACTLY as documented in terrain.ts. `heightAt(body, dir)` without lambdaMin = bilinear interpolation over the 65 x 65 vertex grid of the body's maxRenderLevel tiles, with the vertices evaluated LAZILY one by one and memoised (a query evaluates at most the 4 vertices of its quad; no query ever builds a whole grid), in a bounded cache around callers. `prewarmCollision(body, dir, radius, maxVertices)` evaluates up to maxVertices missing vertices nearest first and returns how many remain (a count budget; no clock). With lambdaMin = analytic evaluation. `normalAt`, `surfaceKind` (ocean body and solid surface below seaLevel), `ensureLoaded` (every tile of every contributing level and layer the height function reads within the radius), `residency` (residentLevel, availableLevel, the fractional effectiveLevel, complete), `elevationRange`.
4. Height function H = D + modifiers + amplification. D is the Catmull-Rom bicubic of the data tiles (using the 1-sample border so it is continuous across tiles and cube faces) blended across the edges of sparse coverage exactly as specified at COVERAGE_BLEND_TILES in terrain.ts: coverage weight w_L (0 on the coverage boundary, 1 a quarter tile inside, smootherstep of the distance to the nearest missing neighbour tile, neighbours across cube edges found through dirToTile), D_L = D_(L-1) + w_L (bicubic_L - D_(L-1)), and the same recursion on the level number for the effective level E. w_L and E are pure functions of the manifest. While a contributing level is not yet resident its term is skipped and residency().complete is false. Terrain modifiers: BodyDef.terrain.modifiers plus a flattenDisc derived from every LaunchSiteDef on that body (inside flatRadius = pad elevation, smoothstep to natural terrain at blendRadius; padElevation 'terrain' samples the natural height at the centre).
5. Band-limited procedural amplification, registry keyed by BodyDef.terrain.amplification.model, with 'earth-landcover', 'lunar-regolith' and 'none'. Integer-hash 3-D gradient noise on planet-fixed coordinates (seamless across faces), octave wavelengths halving from the data wavelength implied by the EFFECTIVE level E at the point (2 texels of level E, a smooth function of position, so octaves and crater size classes fade across a coverage edge instead of ending at a wall), amplitude from Hurst exponent and local data slope/curvature (multifractal), smooth octave fade as a function of lambdaMin (continuous, never switched). Earth: landcover-driven character (read `landcover` tiles when resident; sand ripples, bare rock/lava ridged, soft relief elsewhere, smooth seabed). Moon: hash-grid craters per diameter octave below 4x the effective data posting down to 0.6 m, each size class weighted smoothly by E, equilibrium size-frequency density, parabolic bowl + raised rim + r^-3 ejecta, freshness distribution weighted to degraded craters; regolith fBm calibrated so RMS slope at 2-8 m baselines matches the real NAC DTM tiles when they exist (write the calibration tool under tools/terrain-core and record the numbers); rocks from a Golombek-Rapp style distribution, denser on fresh ejecta.
6. RockField: `rocksNear(...)` deterministic instances; rocks with radius >= the model's collision threshold are also bumps in H so they collide.
7. TerrainBaker for the renderer's workers (pure, worker-safe): `bakeGeometry(body, key) -> { heights: Float32Array(65*65), hMin, hMax }` at band limit tileSize/32, and `bakeNormalMaterial(body, key) -> { rgba: Uint8Array(256*256*4), slopeScale }` (rg = tanh-encoded slopes in the tile tangent frame at band limit tileSize/128, b = cavity/AO, a = material weight: landcover blend on Earth, crater freshness on the Moon), plus `tileBounds`. Scanline-optimised (lattice coordinates advance by constants; craters gathered per tile first). At maxRenderLevel `bakeGeometry` must return exactly the collision surface vertices.
8. Parameters live in data/defs/terrain/*.amplification.json (yours to extend).

ACCEPTANCE (vitest): synthetic tile sets generated by your own fixture writer (analytic heights encoded with src/core/geo/tileCodec.ts into a temp dir) so tests need no baked data, including a SPARSE set whose regional levels disagree with the global level by tens of metres and one region that straddles a cube edge; plus a suite that runs automatically when data/tiles/moon/manifest.json or data/tiles/earth/manifest.json exists and checks real benchmarks (Moon: Tranquility 0.674N 23.473E about -1925 m, Tycho floor, Aitken basin; Earth: launch-site pad flat within 5 cm over flatRadius). Continuity: |H jump| across tile and cube-face borders below 1 mm at every level; derivative-continuous in lambdaMin (no step when an octave fades in). Coverage edges (synthetic sparse set and, when present, every regional level of the real manifests): H evaluated 1 mm either side of a coverage boundary differs by less than 1 mm at 1,000 points per level, with and without amplification; the slope by central differences over 10 cm changes by less than 0.005 across the boundary; on the boundary H equals the parent-level function to 1e-6 m; crater and octave weights are continuous there; w_L and E do not depend on which tiles are resident. Collision = render: `heightAt(dir)` equals bilinear of `bakeGeometry` at max level to < 1 mm at vertices and < 3 cm anywhere. Lazy collision: the first query in a fresh area performs at most 4 vertex evaluations (instrumented counter) and no single collision query exceeds 0.2 ms; prewarmCollision is deterministic and reduces the remaining count to 0. Determinism: identical results on main thread vs a second provider instance, independent of which coarser tiles were loaded first once `ensureLoaded` resolved, and identical eviction for identical call sequences. Amplification never exceeds one-octave amplitude between consecutive levels (bounded morph). Crater statistics test (count vs size on a 1 km^2 patch within 20% of the target law) and RMS slope test. Rocks: same instances for overlapping queries; collidable rocks raise H. Timings measured and reported: analytic `heightAt` at lambdaMin 100 m under 3 microseconds, cached collision query under 0.5 microseconds, `bakeGeometry` + `bakeNormalMaterial` under 12 ms per tile on this machine (single thread). Memory bounded by the configured budget.

SELF-VERIFY: `npx vitest run src/terrain tests/unit/terrain-core`; a small tool that renders hillshaded PNGs of H at several scales around the lunar landing region, the pad, and ACROSS a coverage edge of each regional level (out/terrain-core/*.png), which you must look at: craters and regolith have to read as real lunar terrain, not noise, and no line, wall or change of texture may be visible where coverage ends.

title: Earth data bake: global and launch-region tile pyramids, water mask, cloud map, site resolution
brief:
PROJECT: true-scale Earth/Moon spaceflight simulator. Repo C:\dev\fable-space-game. BEFORE CODING read in full: PROMPT.txt, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (binding; note section 1 and section 7), docs/PACKAGE_RULES.md, src/core/contracts/terrain.ts, src/core/geo/cubeSphere.ts + tileCodec.ts, tools/bake/common/*.py, and docs/research/earth-data.md (verified source URLs; where it disagrees with ARCHITECTURE - launch site, cube mapping, tile size, encodings, lazy proxy, water mask in alpha - ARCHITECTURE wins).

RULES (full text in docs/PACKAGE_RULES.md, binding): (1) Edit only your ownedPaths (tracked) and write generated data only under data/tiles/earth, data/cache/earth and out/bake/earth (all git-ignored). tools/bake/common is lead-owned shared code: import it (cube.py, frt1.py, layout.py), never copy or modify it; needed changes go to docs/requests/bake-earth-<n>.md and your hand-off. (2) No placeholders or stubs. (3) Python 3.10 in a venv under data/cache/earth/venv; run scripts with `python -I`; treat downloads as untrusted (own directories). Secrets are not needed (no keys). (4) Shared machine: another agent bakes the Moon concurrently and seven others compile and run browser tests - use at most 8 worker processes at BELOW-NORMAL priority (psutil nice / `start /belownormal`), keep your peak disk use (tiles + cache) under 16 GB and delete raw downloads once a layer is baked and verified (final cache under 1 GB). Downloads must be resumable and polite (10-20 req/s for tile services). (5) Git: only `git add <your tracked paths>` + commit; never commit data. (6) Write files with the Write tool (heredocs break on Windows); absolute paths. (7) Finish with docs/handoff/bake-earth.md (what was baked, sources and licences, sizes, timings, verification results, how to re-run or add a region).

SCOPE - produce the `earth` tile set at data/tiles/earth with a valid manifest (use layout.merge_layer / write_manifest; mapping and raster orientation exactly as tools/bake/common/cube.py: column follows u, ROW FOLLOWS v):
1. `height` (frt1-height, 259 x 259, vertex-registered via cube.height_tile_dirs): global levels 0-7 from GEBCO 2025 or ETOPO 2022 15 arc-second (topography + bathymetry as the solid surface), preferred scale 0.5 m; regional levels 8-12 within 100 km of the launch site from AWS Terrarium (z up to 15; 10 m 3DEP in Hawai'i), preferred scales 0.125 m (levels 8-10) and 0.0625 m (11-12). The regional SOURCE is feathered into the upsampled global source over the outer 5 km of the region, so the two never disagree by much where coverage ends (the run-time height authority then blends each level into its parent over the last quarter tile, COVERAGE_BLEND_TILES in terrain.ts: you do not implement that blend, you keep the sources close). Coverage rectangles of every regional level extend at least one tile beyond the area of interest so the pad and the 100 km disc lie more than a quarter tile inside them. Coarser levels are area-averaged from finer ones so the pyramid is self-consistent; borders are sampled from the true neighbouring directions (seamless across tiles and cube faces).
2. `albedo` (webp 256 x 256, OPAQUE RGB, no alpha channel, quality about 90, cell-registered via cube.image_tile_dirs): global 0-7 from Blue Marble Next Generation 500 m (no baked relief shading; one cloud-free month), regional 8-12 from Sentinel-2 cloudless (EOX; CC BY-NC-SA - record it as swappable in a sources file). Colour-match the regional imagery to the global base, and feather the outer 64 texels of the coverage of each regional level to the bilinear upsample of the parent level AS STORED (decode the parent tiles), so a renderer can switch levels at a coverage edge without a seam.
3. `watermask` (frt1-u8 256 x 256, classes { land: 0, water: 255 }, intermediate values for anti-aliased shorelines; same levels and coverage as albedo; same feather rule at regional edges): from the elevation sign, corrected with an independent land/water source where land lies below sea level; at regional levels use the best available coastline. Image tiles never carry a mask in alpha (ARCHITECTURE section 1 row 5).
4. `night` (webp, opaque RGB) global 0-7 from NASA Black Marble 500 m (most tiles are black and a few hundred bytes).
5. `landcover` (frt1-u8, ids = LANDCOVER_CLASS in terrain.ts): global 0-7 from a documented colour/height/latitude classifier, regional 8-12 from ESA WorldCover mapped to those ids.
6. Globals: `cloudCoverage` 8192 x 4096 PNG with channels [coverage, cloudTop] (a real global cloud field snapshot; preferred source the alpha cloud composite named in the research doc, licence caveat recorded and source swappable; fallback the CC BY 4.0 8k map; cloudTop/type derived as described in rendering-design.md section 6), and `albedoLowRes` 1024 x 512 RGB.
7. Region manifest data/defs/regions/earth-ka-lae.json (centre, radii per level, sources) and a generic CLI so a new site or an imagery strip elsewhere is a data-only bake: `python -I tools/bake/earth/bake.py <heights|albedo|watermask|night|landcover|clouds|globals|region|all> [--region <id>]`, resumable and idempotent.
8. Site resolution tool: starting from the nominal 19.10 N 155.50 W, find the nearest location on the Ka'u coast that is at least 600 m from the shoreline, has slope under 4 degrees over a 1 km disc, is at least 15 m above sea level, has open ocean to the east (azimuths 60-130 degrees) and sits on bare lava/sparse scrub (not forest, not built-up); write latDeg/lonDeg/padElevation (a number: natural height at the centre) to data/defs/sites/ka-lae-lc1.location.json. SCOPE - `createMapView(gpu, defs): { view: MapView; feature: RenderFeature }`:
1. Trajectory lines drawn in `drawOverlay` (LDR, after tonemapping, display resolution): adaptive sampling of each Patch conic in anomaly until the screen-space chord error is under 0.3 px (cap 2048 points), positioned relative to the patch body's CURRENT position, with a toggle to draw encounter patches at the body's position at intercept (Patch.bodyPosAtEnd). A patch whose nuEnd - nuStart exceeds 2 pi (a node several revolutions ahead, see the Patch doc comment) is drawn as one ellipse with the node placed at nuEnd modulo 2 pi. Instanced screen-space quads 2.5 px wide with analytic edge anti-aliasing and round joins, per-vertex colour/alpha, dashed style for patches with afterNodeId, fade with time ahead, analytic near-plane clipping, and occlusion by bodies computed analytically (ray-sphere test against each body's radius with a 6 px soft fade) so no depth buffer is needed.
2. What is drawn: current and planned patches of the active vessel through every SOI change; faint orbits of other vessels and debris (conicFromState on their state); each body's orbit about its parent (BodySnapshot.orbit); SOI boundaries as faint circles; body and vessel icons with labels when the object is under 6 px; SURFACE TARGETS from snapshot.surfaceTargets drawn on their bodies in the body-fixed frame (they rotate with the body): the landing target as a pin, recovery zones as circles of their radius lying on the sphere, the launch site as a pad icon, all with the same analytic occlusion (hidden on the far side).
3. Markers as crisp SDF icons at float64-projected positions with constant pixel size and text labels (value + time-to): apoapsis, periapsis, ascending/descending node (relative inclination), SOI enter/exit, impact (with latitude/longitude and the miss distance to the landing target when readouts.landingTarget.predicted exists), atmosphere entry (speed, flight-path angle, vacuum periapsis, latitude/longitude of the entry point), closest approach (separation), maneuver nodes. Impact and entry points are additionally drawn ON the body surface at their body-fixed latitude/longitude. Hover shows details; overlapping labels are de-cluttered.
4. Maneuver-node editing: click on the current or planned trajectory -> 'add maneuver' at that point (true anomaly -> ut via timeSincePeriapsis, on the correct revolution); a gizmo with six handles (prograde/retrograde, normal/antinormal, radial out/in) oriented in the node frame, drag semantics 1 m/s per 10 px along the handle's screen direction, with the modifiers taken from PointerState (shift x0.1, ctrl x10) and rate ramp when held at the end; dragging the node body slides it along the orbit in time; buttons for +/- one orbit (the planned patch must survive: the predictor follows the conic to the node), delete, and a numeric panel (three delta-v components, total, ut) editable by typing; wheel over a handle nudges by 0.1 m/s. Multiple nodes supported. Target selection by clicking a body.
5. `MapView.update(snapshot, camera, commands, pointer, displaySize): MapUpdateResult` is called BEFORE the flight controller and the camera rig with the snapshot and camera of the frame that is on screen; it hit-tests against the same projections used for drawing. `consumed` is true while the pointer hovers an interactive element, during a drag (until release, even if the pointer leaves the element) and while the numeric panel has focus - the app then withholds the pointer from the camera rig and the throttle from the controller. `focus` is set on the frame the player double-clicks a body or vessel (PointerState.doubleClick). `describe()` reports screen positions of markers, nodes, handles and surface targets for tests.
6. A unit test asserts continuity (each patch's end position in ROOT equals the next patch's start within 1 m at the shared time).
7. Browser spec with the synthetic scene: the full Earth -> Moon -> Earth chain, at-intercept drawing, every marker kind and both nodes appear (asserted through describe()) and are screenshotted. Screenshots in out/screens/map-view reviewed by eye: thin crisp lines, readable markers, an uncluttered gizmo. SCOPE - `createSkyFeature(ctx): RenderFeature`:
1. Stars from data/sky (SkyManifest): instanced points drawn in `drawBackground` where depth is zero (depth read-only, compare equal); each star is a Gaussian PSF (sigma about 0.7 px, stable under TAA jitter) whose pixel luminances integrate to its illuminance divided by the pixel solid angle, coloured from the catalogue, multiplied by frame exposure and written through writeHdr; directions are ROOT (J2000 equatorial) axes so the sky rotates correctly as seen from a rotating body. 2. Milky Way and faint-star background from the rgb9e5 cube with its mip chain, scaled by `luminanceScale`.

Sun disc drawn analytically at its true angular size with per-channel limb darkening from BodyDef.emission, luminance = illuminance / (pi sin^2 theta), written through writeHdr (it saturates at HDR_MAX at every exposure; that is intended and tested); partial occultation by bodies handled by depth.

GGX prefilter to 5 mips (amortised) and SH9 projection; publish 'env.probeCube' and 'env.sh9'. 1. Wave field = analytic swell + FFT chop. Port `oceanSwellHeight` to WGSL with phases prepared in float64 on the CPU each frame so it is exact in float32 anywhere on the planet, including horizontal displacement and analytic normals for those components. On top, a Tessendorf FFT in compute: 4 cascades of 256^2 with patch lengths 8192/7, /29, /113, /449 m sampled triplanar in planet-fixed coordinates modulo 8192 m, JONSWAP spectrum with directional spreading from OceanRenderDef wind, HIGH-PASSED so wavelengths above about 25 m carry no energy (the long waves are the swell, which physics shares), TMA depth attenuation near shore; outputs displacement, slopes and Jacobian, published as 'ocean.displacement' and 'ocean.derivatives'; foam from Jacobian folding with temporal decay.
2. The shared water shading function, registered as the `brdf_water` override so the deferred far water and your forward near pass produce identical radiance where they meet: GGX with F0 0.02 and roughness from resolved normals plus UNRESOLVED slope variance (everything filtered out at the pixel footprint, up to the Cox-Munk limit 0.003 + 0.00512 * U10) - one formula that yields the broad sun glint seen from orbit and the tight glitter path at the surface; sky reflection from 'env.probeCube' / 'atmosphere.skyViewLut' with horizon roughness fade; sun reflection attenuated by transmittance, eclipse and cloud shadow; body colour from single scattering with per-channel absorption, tinted by the imagery colour already in the G-buffer (turquoise shelves, deep-ocean blue); depth-dependent seabed visibility from `decodeWaterDepth(RT2.a)` in the deferred path.

Displacement, refraction and depth-based foam fade to exactly zero by fadeStart; between fadeStart and fadeEnd the forward surface is the flat sea-level surface shaded by the same brdf_water with the G-buffer's encoded depth semantics, drawn with opacity falling smoothly from 1 to 0 over the already-lit deferred sheet (small constant depth bias toward the eye so the coplanar surfaces never z-fight). 4. FRAME-GRAPH RULES FOR YOU (ARCHITECTURE 10.0, 10.3): half-resolution ray-marched volumes (plumes, pad smoke, exhaust trails, reentry plasma, fireballs) are rendered in `preTransparent(frame, encoder)` into your own targets, depth-tested per sample against THIS frame's 'scene.depth' / 'scene.depthHalf', then composited in `drawTransparent` with the core's depth-aware upsample (in-scatter + transmittance; dual-source blending where the transmittance is coloured). Nine-engine cluster interaction (merged plume downstream). Each active engine or cluster registers a capsule light (FrameContext.lights) with intensity proportional to thrust so pad, smoke, lunar ground and the vehicle's aft are lit.
2. Exhaust in the atmosphere: lit volumetric trail along the flight path, contrail formation in the cold upper troposphere, expanding and fading by wind-free diffusion.
3.
